scenes.title: Western New York in 1815
scenes.assetBrief: Modern USGS locator selected for geographic accuracy. It shows Lake Erie, Lake Ontario and Chautauqua Lake, with a georeferenced Hanover town reference point on land; Edward's exact birth site is unknown.
scenes.place: Hanover, Chautauqua County, New York • 17 August 1815

scenes.title: Edward and Caroline
scenes.assetBrief: Rights-cleared 1839 David H. Burr atlas context for the year Edward and Caroline married. New York, Ohio, Illinois and Missouri are identified as named regions from their early family years; no connecting line is shown, and neither an exact route nor a marriage place is claimed.
scenes.place: Married 21 December 1839 • exact marriage place not claimed

scenes.title: The Webb family in Illinois
scenes.assetBrief: Authentic public-domain daguerreotype of Nauvoo circa 1846, showing homes, work yards, residents and the completed temple on the hill. The image is attributed to Lucian R. Foster, although authorship is not definitive; no visible person is identified as Edward or another Webb relative.

scenes.title: A family moving west
scenes.assetBrief: Public-domain crop of Benjamin Franklin Reinhart's 1867 painting An Evening Halt—Emigrants Moving to the West in 1840. It is a later historical rendering of the family's era and material world, not an eyewitness Webb scene; no depicted person, wagon, animal, route or event is identified with the Webb family. The separate Illinois–Missouri county-conflict map remains supporting evidence rather than the narrative visual.
scenes.place: American westward migration context • represented as 1840

scenes.title: The Uriah Curtis Company
scenes.assetBrief: The 4 July 1852 company report lists Edward Milo Webb, Caroline Amelia Webb, Mary Jane Webb, Cordelia, Marcellus, Edward Jr. and young Caroline as a traveling household. James Hofer appears on the following manuscript page and is not visible here.
scenes.place: Uriah Curtis's 16th Company of 50 • report dated 4 July 1852

scenes.title: The journey ends beside the Platte
scenes.assetBrief: Albert Bierstadt's 1859 wood engraving Crossing the Platte provides near-period emigrant and South Platte context. Published seven years after Edward's death, it does not depict his company or death, and no figure is identified as a Webb relative.

scenes.title: The family continues west
scenes.assetBrief: Salt Lake City as represented in 1850, two years before Caroline arrived with the children. The engraving shows the settlement at their destination but does not depict the Webb family or their arrival.
scenes.place: Salt Lake City as represented in 1850 • family arrived September 1852

scenes.title: Approaching the proof frontier
scenes.assetBrief: Edward Milo Webb Sr.'s supported relationship to James Webb Jr. and Hannah Griswold remains illuminated. The generations above James Jr. dim because the proposed parent couple and deeper ancestry remain unresolved.
scenes.place: Webb proof frontier • supported line through James Webb Jr.
